newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: CHAMBER CALLS FOR INTEREST RATE CUT
The Australian Business Chamber has called for a further interest rate, after Australia's official jobless rate for December rose to a seasonally adjusted 8-point-6 percent.
The Chamber is particularly disturbed by the level of youth unemployment, which is the now the worst it's been in two-and-a-half years at 30-point-4 per cent.
It says changes are needed in the education system to make school-leavers more attractive to employers.
Policy Manager Paul Orton says the government's jobless rate target of 8-and-a-quarter per cent by June is unlikely to be met, nor the employment growth goal of one-and-a-half per cent.
TAMWORTH COUNTRY MUSIC FESTIVAL KICKS OFF TODAY
As many as 50-thousand visitors are expected at Tamworth in the north-west of New South Wales, for the start of the annual Country Music Festival.
The 10-day festival begins today.
Already hotels, motels and caravan parks are full, while temporary camping grounds have been set up in school playgrounds, on sporting fields and elsewhere.
All the big names of Country Music have arrived, while buskers already line the main business area.
The festival concludes the weekend after next with the National Country Music Awards.
BISHOP SAYS BELLO ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT THWARTED
Local people reportedly thwarted an attempt to assassinate East Timorese leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner, Archbishop Carlos Bello, last month.
Auxiliary Bishop of Melbourne, Hilton Deakin, says the assassination was to take place outside a Dili cathedral, but was thwarted by locals who heard about the plot.
An Indonesia soldier was reportedly paid to carry out the assassination.
An East Timorese Catholic contacted Bishop Deakin this week, saying the soldier was killed before getting to Archbishop Bello, and was found with Indonesian rupiah worth many thousands of dollars.
Bishop Deakin told ABC Radio the assassin talked about the plan outside the Cathedral, and was overheard by some locals.
ACTING CHAIRMAN SAYS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS ORGANISED
The Acting Chairman of the Torres Strait Regional Authority claims an organised ring is helping illegal immigrants into Australia.
Terry Waia, who's also the chairman of Saibai Island, found four men in his island village yesterday, who claimed they were Iraqi Nationals.
Mr Waia says these people aren't travelling to Australia by themselves, and believes they're getting help from someone.
FISCHER SAYS JOBLESS RATE A HICCUP
Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer says he's confident the Government's schemes to bolster small business and create more jobs are kicking in.
Mr Fischer says the small rise in unemployment is just a hiccup in the statistics, and the Government's well on its way to lowering the jobless rate.
Touring regional Queensland, Mr Fischer says the Federal Government is determined to do what it can to maximise job creation.
He says it's trying to create the framework to achieve that, including lowering interest rates to give more small business the confidence to create extra jobs.
SYDNEY HARBOUR RACE PORT OF CALL
Sydney Harbour will be a port of call for the international yacht race, the Whitbread Round the World Race, in December.
The Whitbread race will start in Southampton, England in September, with yachts arriving in Sydney around the 22nd of December, and departing on January the fourth.
Premier Bob Carr says the economic and tourism benefits for Sydney and New South Wales will be enormous.
NSW ATTORNEY-GENERAL TO MEDIATE IN JOCKEY DISPUTE
The state Attorney-General is to mediate in the jockeys pay dispute, after talks yesterday failed to secure a better pay deal for New South Wales riders.
The union representing jockeys, the AWU, says jockeys are currently paid A$70 a race and are asking for an increase to A$130.
The AWU's John Longhurst says during talks yesterday chaired by Racing Minister Richard Face, the union indicated jockeys would accept a new pay deal of A$90 a race.
But he says the AJC, representing owners and trainers, was not prepared to consider going above A$80.
Mr Longhurst says jockeys are disappointed at the lack of a compromise deal and will no have to wait for the Attorney-General to mediate to resolve the dispute.
MORE PROTECTION WANTED FOR LANDOWNERS OVER WIK
The Pastoralists' and Graziers' Association of Western Australia wants a better system of protecting landowners from losing money on land devalued by the state planning process.

Association President Tony Boultbee says the Peel draft plan, the first of a series of new planning initiatives in rural Western Australia, has already adversely affected the value of hundreds of farming properties in the region.
Mr Boultbee says the Association this week met with the Premier and his new Ministers, Graham Kierath and Kim Hames to put their case.
He says the Premier promised to investigate current procedures for reserving and acquiring private property.
Mr Boultbee says the Premier and his Ministers also agreed to further investigate how landowners were currently being disadvantaged by the state's planning procedures.
